name: Epitalon
lead: Epitalon, also spelled epithalon or epithalone, is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the amino acid sequence alanine-glutamic acid-aspartic acid-glycine (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, AEDG) and the molecular formula C14H22N4O9.[1] It was designed from the amino acid composition of epithalamin, an extract of bovine pineal gland, and has been described as the putative active component of that preparation.[1][2] Most of the research on epitalon and epithalamin comes from the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, led by Vladimir Khavinson, although laboratories elsewhere have recently begun to study it.[1]

In looksmaxxing and longevity circles it is discussed as a way to look and stay younger. Users describe it as a telomere and pineal-gland peptide that might slow cellular ageing, improve sleep through melatonin rhythms, and keep skin and appearance youthful over the long term, an ageing-focused approach that sits alongside skin, hair and body-composition work rather than a direct cosmetic product.[25][26] Laboratory work reports that it increases telomere length in human cell lines through telomerase upregulation or an alternative lengthening mechanism,[3] and Russian clinical reports claim effects on ageing markers.[1][4] Independent, large, placebo-controlled human trials have not been published, and a 2026 narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence for the synthetic peptide separately from the older extract.[4]

Epitalon is not approved as a drug by major regulators and is sold as a research chemical, usually as a freeze-dried powder for injection or nasal use.[5] On looksmax.org and T Nation it appears in peptide stacks discussed by members using unregulated products, an area in which product quality is not independently verified.[22][23][25]

paras: Epitalon is a short linear peptide made of alanine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid and glycine.[1][5] Grokipedia states it is produced by solid-phase peptide synthesis, that a Russian patent issued in 2001 described synthesis of such tissue-specific peptides, and that its short length makes it prone to degradation in solution, so it is typically lyophilised for storage.[5] Epithalamin, the extract it was derived from, is a chemically distinct pineal-derived polypeptide preparation.[4]

Epithalamin was isolated from bovine pineal glands by Khavinson and V. N. Anisimov, with Grokipedia giving 1973 and describing the work as growing from Soviet-era military gerontology at the Kirov Military Medical Academy in Leningrad.[5] Khavinson founded the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology in 1992, and the AEDG tetrapeptide was identified from epithalamin's amino acid analysis and synthesised around the early 1990s; Grokipedia itself gives both late 1980s and early 1990s for the development, so exact dates are uncertain.[5]

A 2002 review described a technology for manufacturing complex peptide preparations from tissue extracts, with the pineal preparation epithalamin augmenting growth of pineal explants in vitro.[2] A 2000 paper reported an increase in the lifespan of Drosophila exposed to epitalon during development, and 2001 and 2002 papers reported effects in senescent monkeys, tumour-prone mice, rats and retinitis pigmentosa models.[6][13][11][12][15]

The compound's profile outside Russia grew in the 2000s and 2010s through anti-ageing literature and peptide vendors. A 2003 study of human fibroblasts reported telomerase induction, and recent years have seen studies from other laboratories, including work on telomere length in human cell lines in 2025 and a registered 2026 early-phase study.[1][3][19] Looksmax.org and T Nation threads in the 2020s show it entering peptide stacks discussed for appearance and longevity.[23][25]

Vladimir Khavinson was born on 27 November 1946 in Cottbus, Germany, and died on 6 January 2024 in Saint Petersburg.[24] A Russian gerontologist and colonel of the medical service, he directed the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, headed the gerontology chair at North-Western State Medical University and received the Order of Friendship in 2016.[24]

Wikipedia credits him with the concept of peptide bioregulators, short peptides he described as regulators of ageing, and with a practice he called bioregulating peptide therapy. The same article lists six peptide-based medicines associated with him, including Thymalin, Epithalamin, Cortexin and Retinalamin, and says they were first used mainly by military medical services.[24] That article notes that its account relies heavily on his own publications and patents and carries a maintenance notice about promotional content, and the epitalon article on Wikipedia likewise notes that much of the evidence comes from the originating group.[24][1]

Wikipedia reports that epitalon appeared to induce telomere elongation through increased telomerase activity in human fibroblast cultures, extending their proliferative capacity beyond the Hayflick limit in one experiment, and that it decondensed heterochromatin in lymphocytes from elderly donors and reduced production of the protein MMP9 in ageing skin fibroblasts.[1] A 2025 Biogerontology study reported that epitalon increases telomere length in human cell lines through telomerase upregulation or ALT activity.[3] Group reports also describe epigenetic effects on gene expression and protein synthesis during neurogenesis,[7] antioxidant properties of pineal peptides,[8] restoration of pineal and pancreatic hormonal functions,[9] and effects on proliferative activity and inflammatory pathways in a monocyte cell line.[10]

Whether these effects occur at meaningful levels in living humans after injection or nasal use has not been established by independent studies. Grokipedia notes that epitalon is proposed to influence melatonin synthesis and that animal results on lifespan have been mixed.[5]

In animals, researchers report lifespan extension in fruit flies,[6] reduced spontaneous mammary tumours in HER-2/neu transgenic mice,[11] inhibition of colon carcinogenesis induced by dimethylhydrazine in rats,[12] and restoration of disturbed neuroendocrine regulation in senescent monkeys.[13] A study of stressors and antistressors on lifespan in HER-2/neu mice is also cited.[14] Wikipedia additionally cites reduced chromosomal aberrations in ageing mice, increased antioxidant enzymes in rats and reduced tumour counts in C3H/He mice.[1] Epitalon preserved retinal function in a rat model of retinitis pigmentosa,[15] protected mouse oocytes from post-ovulatory ageing in vitro,[16] enhanced delayed wound healing in an in vitro model of diabetic retinopathy,[17] and improved maturation and embryo development in bovine oocytes.[18] These findings come from cell and animal systems.
ClinicalTrials.gov lists an early phase 1 study of systemic and topical geroprotective rejuvenation assessed with ageing clocks (n=48), enrolling by invitation with a start date in October 2026.[19]

The human literature on epitalon is small and comes mainly from Russian groups. Wikipedia summarises reports that epitalon and epithalamin each increased telomere length in blood cells of patients aged 60 to 65 and 75 to 80 with comparable efficacy, that they appeared to restore melatonin secretion in aged monkeys and humans, that a trial in retinitis pigmentosa found a positive clinical effect in 90 percent of treated patients, and that in tuberculosis patients epitalon did not correct existing chromosomal aberrations but appeared to protect against new ones.[1][15] The retinitis pigmentosa paper is a controlled clinical trial that also reports effects in a rat model.[15]

Wikipedia also cites prospective cohort studies of epithalamin, the extract, and not synthetic epitalon: a cohort of 266 people over age 60 in which treatment was associated with a 1.6 to 1.8 fold reduction in mortality over six years, with larger reductions when combined with thymalin, and a cohort of 79 coronary patients over more than 12 years with lower cardiovascular and overall mortality.[1] Grokipedia describes limited human studies mainly from the same group and states that broader clinical validation, including independent phase 1 safety studies, remains necessary.[5] A 2025 review and a 2026 narrative review assess the mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence,[4][20] and a 2026 gerontology review places epitalon among peptide therapeutics for healthy ageing.[21] No independent randomised placebo-controlled trial of epitalon for ageing or appearance outcomes was found.

The 2026 narrative review reports that human studies are limited to small physiological or biomarker trials plus an older controlled study in retinitis pigmentosa, and states that no adequately powered randomized trial has established therapeutic efficacy.[4] A 2026 ClinicalTrials.gov registration lists an early phase 1 study of 48 participants on geroprotective rejuvenation assessed by ageing clocks, enrolling by invitation.[19]

Grokipedia reports no severe adverse events in long-term Russian trials of related preparations and low toxicity in preclinical data, while emphasising that independent clinical validation is lacking.[5] Because telomerase activity is also a feature of many cancers, researchers and commentators discuss theoretical concerns about telomerase-activating compounds, although animal studies from the originating group report reduced rather than increased tumour incidence.[11][12][1] Epitalon is sold as an unregulated research chemical, so product identity, purity and sterility are not covered by regulatory oversight. Grokipedia describes reported human adverse events as few and mostly mild injection-site reactions, again mainly from the originating group, and says use in pregnancy is contraindicated and lactation data are lacking.[5]

Grokipedia states that epitalon is approved by neither the US FDA nor the European Medicines Agency for any use and is treated as a research chemical in the US and EU, while epithalamin and related pineal preparations have limited approvals in Russia for conditions such as menopause-related symptoms and anovulatory infertility.[5] It also reports that the FDA has barred compounding pharmacies from using the peptide, describes a 2026 HHS draft enforcement-discretion policy covering compounding of epitalon and five other peptides that it says does not make the peptide an approved drug, and says Health Canada seized unauthorised injectable epitalon from an online seller in August 2025 citing infection and allergy risks.[5] These regulatory details come from Grokipedia, which can contain errors.

The 2026 narrative review states that oncologic, immunogenicity, product-quality and regulatory questions remain open after a 2026 FDA advisory review, and concludes that the peptide is biologically active but clinically unproven; it calls for standardised pharmacologic, safety and disease-specific studies before clinical use.[4]

On looksmax.org, long guide-style threads present epitalon as an overlooked anti-ageing compound. One introductory thread frames it as a way to extend lifespan and gain benefits sought by people trying to stay youthful, lists sections on mechanism, benefits, risks and safety, and administration, and cites telomerase activation as its core mechanism; its author adds a disclaimer that it is not medical advice.[25] Other users reply with enthusiasm or sceptical one-liners.[25][26]

On T Nation, epitalon appears in short threads about peptides alongside testosterone replacement, where posters credit it with cognitive effects or ask how it fits among other peptides.[22][23] These accounts are user reports and are not controlled data. Product identity, purity and sterility for products sold online are not covered by regulatory oversight.[5]

Epitalon is sold by peptide vendors for research use and discussed in anti-ageing communities as a telomere peptide and pineal bioregulator. Community discussion is covered in the section on looksmaxxing communities; popularity in biohacking circles has been described as outpacing clinical evidence, and Grokipedia reports online sales through gray markets with variable quality.[5]

timeline.event: Vladimir Khavinson is born in Cottbus, Germany.[24]
Epithalamin, a bovine pineal extract, is first isolated by Khavinson and Anisimov, per Grokipedia.[5]
Khavinson founds the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology.[5]
The tetrapeptide AEDG (epitalon) is identified and synthesised from epithalamin's amino acid composition.[5]
A study reports that epitalon increased lifespan of Drosophila melanogaster.[6]
Reports of effects in a retinitis pigmentosa model and trial, and in tumour-prone mice and rats, are published.[15][11][12]
Human fibroblast study reports telomerase induction and extended proliferative capacity, per Wikipedia.[1]
Khavinson receives the Russian Order of Friendship.[24]
A Biogerontology study reports telomere lengthening in human cell lines; Health Canada seizure of unauthorised injectable epitalon is reported by Grokipedia.[3][5]
A narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence for epitalon, and an early phase 1 study is registered.[4][19]

lore.intro: In anti-ageing and peptide communities epitalon is described as a telomere-lengthening pineal peptide; on looksmax.org guide threads present it as an overlooked youth-preserving compound, and on T Nation it appears in short peptide-stack threads and is credited with cognitive and longevity benefits.[22][23][25]

claims.claim: Epitalon lengthens telomeres and slows ageing
claims.believers: Proponents cite Khavinson-group reports of telomerase activation and increased telomere length in cells and in blood cells of older patients.[1][3]
claims.experts: The cell-line result was reported in 2025, but reviews note that most data come from one research group and that independent human trials are lacking; a 2026 narrative review evaluates mechanistic, preclinical and clinical evidence separately.[3][4][5]

claims.believers: Supporters point to Russian cohort studies showing lower mortality in older people given the pineal extract.[1]
claims.experts: Those cohorts used epithalamin, the extract, rather than synthetic epitalon, and were not independent randomised trials; animal lifespan results are mixed according to Grokipedia.[1][5]

claims.claim: Epitalon improves cognition and brain function
claims.believers: A T Nation poster says it improves firing of prefrontal cortex neurones and wakes quiescent ones.[22]
claims.experts: Group publications report effects on gene expression during neurogenesis in cell systems; no controlled human cognition trial was found.[7]

claims.claim: Epitalon is anti-cancer, or alternatively could promote cancer via telomerase
claims.believers: Some supporters cite the mouse and rat studies showing fewer spontaneous mammary tumours and colon tumours.[11][12]
claims.experts: Those findings come from the originating group in animals; the theoretical concern about telomerase activation has not been tested in human trials of epitalon.[1][5]

claims.claim: Epitalon repairs sleep and melatonin rhythms
claims.believers: Supporters describe it as a pineal bioregulator that restores melatonin secretion.[1]
claims.experts: Wikipedia reports restored melatonin secretion in aged monkeys and humans in group studies; independent replication was not found.[1][13]

claims.claim: Epitalon is an overlooked compound for staying youthful with minimal side effects
claims.believers: A looksmax.org guide frames it as a low-risk way to defy ageing, built on telomerase activation.[25]
claims.experts: Reviews describe the peptide as biologically active but clinically unproven, with safety data mostly from the originating group.[4][5]

claims.claim: Epitalon products sold online are what they claim to be
claims.believers: Users discuss sourcing and stacking it with other peptides.[22][23]
claims.experts: Grokipedia reports that quality and purity vary in gray markets and that Health Canada seized unauthorised injectable product in 2025.[5]

angle.text: People who use epitalon aim at general anti-ageing rather than a single cosmetic change, hoping that slower cellular ageing and better sleep show up as younger-looking skin and energy. This outcome is a claim made by users and vendors; cell studies report effects such as lower MMP9 production in ageing skin fibroblasts, but no trial has measured appearance outcomes.[1][25]

card.summary: A synthetic pineal peptide discussed for anti-ageing, with users hoping slower cellular ageing keeps skin and overall look youthful.
card.note: Not approved by major regulators; sold as a research chemical with unverified product quality.

quick.overview:
Epitalon is a four-amino-acid peptide developed in Russia from a pineal gland extract. People discuss it for anti-ageing, hoping it keeps skin, sleep and overall appearance youthful.

Cell studies report telomerase activation and longer telomeres, and animal studies report longer lifespan in some models. Human data are small and come mostly from the originating Vladimir Khavinson group [1][4].
quick.how: It is sold as a research peptide, typically a lyophilised powder for injection or nasal use, and appears in looksmax.org and T Nation threads as part of peptide stacks aimed at longevity and appearance. Users describe it as a long-term anti-ageing approach rather than a quick cosmetic change [22][25].
quick.risks: No major regulator has approved it. Product identity, purity and sterility are unverified, and Health Canada seized unauthorised injectable product in 2025, per Grokipedia. Researchers discuss a theoretical concern about telomerase activation and cancer, while animal studies from the originating group report fewer tumours [5][11][12].
